summary: This June 24 Dante #9 source extends the Dante cluster by making Purgatory a reversal of Hell's frozen imagination: Virgil must be washed off, time returns as emotional cleansing, heart and desire matter more than ritual form, and mass society appears as the modern system that forces imagination into managed hierarchy.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Cato's command to wash Dante's face becomes a metaphor for cleansing Virgil's infernal influence, because Virgil has fed Dante lies about Hell and must be removed from the ascent.
existing_lens_links.rationale: This is the cleanest existing Guide Trap link: Virgil remains necessary for passage, but the active mechanism is the guide's own infernal grammar contaminating the person he guides.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Purgatory has time, day, night, dreams, waiting, climbing, and emotional duration because the soul must actively learn, meditate, cleanse itself, and serve its time rather than remain frozen in Hell.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The source directly extends Free Will's Purgatory anchor from self-forgiveness into temporal agency: ascent requires lived duration, practice, and emotional time.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Dante's exact Purgatory geography becomes a treasure map for imagination, letting a reader reconstruct real ascent through beaches, terraces, sun, stars, bodies, and paths rather than consume symbolic summary.
existing_lens_links.rationale: Poetry owns the positive reader-access mechanism when Dante's spatial precision trains imagination into a walkable spiritual world.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: The Cato and baptism questions make heart, will, and desire the deeper criterion beneath outward religious timing or ritual status.
existing_lens_links.rationale: Love Recognizes owns this only where the mechanism is inward recognition of a soul's orientation; Free Will owns the agency burden, and Religion As Administrative Filter owns office or ritual administration.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: A student asks whether open imagination can survive organized society, and Jiang answers through Dante's disgust at cities where people become isolated cogs, lose roots, and need bureaucracy, hierarchy, and inequality to function.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The mass-society link should stay narrow: this is about scale forcing social imagination and identity loss, not the digital-control grid.

The guide's success in getting Dante out of Hell does not make him clean; Cato's command exposes that Dante must remove Virgil's infernal influence before ascent can begin.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Guide Trap owns Virgil when mediation itself contaminates the learner. Poetry owns Dante's spatial method; Free Will owns the soul's active cleansing; Love Recognizes owns inward recognition.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold for a future Free Will compression: Hell is timeless stasis, while Purgatory restores emotional time, day/night rhythm, dreaming, waiting, and climbable practice. Agency returns as duration that must be lived through rather than a single decision.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Free Will owns time, cleansing, and agency. Poetry owns the map that makes ascent imaginable; Religion owns ritual administration only when office, baptism, or sacramental gatekeeping is the active mechanism.

new_lens_seeds.title: Purgatory As Imagination Map
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: A reader can move spiritually only when a work gives enough concrete geography, rhythm, time, and embodied action for ascent to become imaginable rather than merely asserted.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The mechanism could connect Dante's mountain, Jiang's teaching method, reader visions, living-school practice, and public lens design, but this source alone still fits inside Poetry and Free Will.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: Hold as a seed only. Do not create a public Purgatory page unless later sources show the map-making mechanism cannot be held by Poetry plus Free Will.

chronology_notes.note: Dated 2026-06-24, this source follows the same-day Dante #8 Inferno cluster and marks the transition from frozen Hell to Purgatory's emotional time, day/night rhythm, dreams, waiting, and climbable agency.

This source gives the strongest current Purgatory-side Virgil boundary: after the guide's Hell work succeeds, the first ascent ritual can still be read as cleansing Dante of Virgil's lies and influence.

The Cato and baptism exchanges clarify a late-June Dante formulation: inward heart, will, and desire are treated as deeper than chronology or ritual form, while the lecture leaves the theological paradox unresolved rather than promoting a settled doctrinal rule.

The closing question gives a June 24 Dante classroom version of mass-society pressure: at sufficient scale, organized society forces people to imagine the system as meaningful while bureaucracy, hierarchy, inequality, and schooling strip roots and identity.
